findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is exposed as a GET route in config/routes.rb and immediately changes the current user's notification level before rendering the Ember unsubscribe page. A logged-in browser therefore mutates state on any GET, with no confirmation or CSRF token: mail-scanner/link prefetching, a page refresh, or an tag on a third-party site can trigger it. It is also non-idempotent: watching/tracking is first downgraded to regular, and a second visit to the same email link then downgrades regular to muted, so merely reopening the confirmation page further changes the user's settings than the original click intended.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never visited or interacted with the topic, for example when an email link is opened while logged in as a different account than the recipient. The next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating a TopicUser record at the desired level (as TopicUser.change would) or handling the no-subscription case.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses the canonical TopicUser.change update path
findings.body: The action assigns notification_level directly and calls tu.save!, bypassing TopicUser.change (used by TopicsController#set_notifications). TopicUser.change is the path that stamps notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id=user_changed and publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change message. Direct assignment leaves the change metadata stale and means other open clients showing this topic are not updated to the new notification level until reload.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url but MessageBuilder provides no fallback
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder#body (line 90) and #html_part (line 67) render that string whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder supplies defaults for site_name/base_url/user_preferences_url but not unsubscribe_url, and only UserNotifications#send_notification_email passes it. Any other existing caller that builds mail with add_unsubscribe_link: true alone (previously valid, as the old spec did) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument for unsubscribe_url and fail to send. The builder should only append the per-topic sentence when unsubscribe_url is present, or provide a safe fallback.

findings.title: New unsubscribe behaviour has no meaningful test coverage
findings.body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to the message_with_unsubscribe fixture; no example asserts that the per-topic URL actually appears in the text body or HTML part, and the PR adds no controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all. The slug-mismatch redirect, the watching/tracking->regular and regular->muted transitions, repeat-visit behaviour, anonymous access, and the missing-TopicUser case are therefore all untested and could regress silently.
